user.title: Custom Branding
user.description: Put your icons in a folder inside the Home Assistant configuration directory (for example {default_dir}, which becomes /config/{default_dir}). File names must match the ones Home Assistant uses: favicon.ico, favicon-192x192.png, favicon-512x512.png, maskable_icon-512x512.png, logo-loading.svg, and so on. See the README for the full list.

data_description.brand_name: Replaces "Home Assistant" in the browser tab and in the name of the installed app.
data_description.assets_dir: Path relative to the configuration directory. Keep it outside custom_components, which HACS replaces on every update.
data_description.patch_html: Off by default. The login and onboarding pages have no extension point, so their title can only be changed by rewriting files inside the frontend package. The integration keeps a backup and reapplies the change on every start, so it survives an image update.

error.empty_name: The brand name cannot be empty.
error.empty_dir: The asset folder cannot be empty.
error.dir_not_found: Folder not found inside the configuration directory.
error.no_assets: No recognised file in that folder. File names must match the ones Home Assistant uses, such as favicon.ico or favicon-512x512.png.

init.title: Custom Branding
init.description: Changing anything here reloads the integration. Replacing an icon on disk with the same file name only needs the custom_branding.apply action.
